paper_title: TRUTH DECAY Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models
caption: Average Change Per Followup, Claude MMLU-Pro. When a LLM originally answers incorrectly, it experiences up to 40% higher change percentages than when it has an initially correct answer.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the answer change percentage by initial accuracy across multiple turns, comparing two different initial answer types. The x-axis is labeled "Turn Number" and features a linear scale ranging from 1 to 7, with numeric tick marks placed at intervals of 1. The y-axis is labeled "Average Change Percentage (%)" and utilizes a linear scale with tick marks ranging from 10 to 50 at regular intervals of 10. The plot contains two solid lines, both marked with circular data points. The solid red line, representing an "Initial Correct Answer," starts at approximately 4% at Turn 1, increases slightly to roughly 6% at Turn 2, remains flat at Turn 3, rises to near 12% at Turn 4, and then maintains a steady, horizontal trend at that value through to Turn 7. The solid orange line, representing an "Initial Incorrect Answer," begins at approximately 16.5% at Turn 1, rises to roughly 24.5% at Turn 2, stays flat at Turn 3, sharply increases to peak at approximately 49% at Turn 4, and subsequently remains steady at 49% through the end of the x-axis at Turn 7.
